title: Control Evidence Concierge: Regionalization & Audit Playback
creator: Sofia Nguyen
description:
Background: Auditors increasingly ask for deterministic evidence packages (logs, config snapshots, KMS proofs) scoped to a jurisdiction and retention window. Our existing collectors and indexers produce artifacts, but there is no unified, queryable 'concierge' that assembles a jurisdictional evidence bundle and allows auditors to 'play back' system state for a point-in-time during the retention window.

Goal: Ship a minimal viable "Concierge" service that can: (1) assemble region-scoped evidence bundles for SOC 2 / ISO 27001 controls; (2) simulate retention window queries to show what artifacts would be returned given current retention policy; (3) provide an auditor-friendly export (signed manifest + links or archived bundle) and audit-playback UI endpoint in Console.

Scope: Product-level orchestration and UX for evidence bundles, control-to-artifact mapping, a retention-simulator API, and lightweight audit-playback endpoints. Implementation will reuse existing collectors (evidence harvester, telemetry normalizer) and Console storage/links. We will NOT re-implement new collectors or change retention stores in this ticket; those are separate ENG tickets.

Success metrics:
- Ability to produce a signed evidence bundle for 90% of SOC 2 control mappings within 10 minutes for a single region.
- Retention simulator accuracy within ±1 day compared to authoritative retention policies for sampled queries.
- Auditor export (zip + signed manifest) format accepted by at least two enterprise customers in pilot.

Design / Proposed approach:
1) Control mapping catalog: a curated mapping of SOC 2 / ISO controls to artifact types (logs, config snapshots, audit logs, policy docs). Store as a versioned YAML in Confluence + backing index in Console metadata.
2) Regionalization layer: query collectors by region tag and tenant residency. If an artifact is cross-region, mark and include reason.
3) Retention simulator: deterministic engine that, given a retention policy, time range, and artifact metadata (created_at, last_modified, retention_label), returns the set of artifacts that would exist. Used for both preflight checks and auditor queries.
4) Evidence bundle assembly: fetch artifact metadata, validate signatures where available (KMS thumbprints), generate a signed manifest (hashes + provenance), and produce export-able archive or grant time-limited Console link.
5) Audit-playback UI: simple streaming view to step through manifest entries, show artifact previews, and play back sequence for incident timelines.

Tradeoffs / Constraints:
- Real-time vs snapshot: real-time assembly is slower but more accurate; snapshots are faster. MVP will default to snapshot with explicit "live-check" option.
- PII: Some artifacts contain PII; bundles will include redaction flags and do not package raw PII unless customer explicitly permits (opt-in).
- Security: sign manifests using customer-specific KMS keys when available. If not, use platform signing with explicit audit trail.

Milestones / Tasks:
- Define control-to-artifact mapping and store (PM lead) (W1).
- Build retention simulator prototype (ENG) (W1-2).
- Implement bundle assembler service that composes manifests (ENG) (W2-3).
- Console: export UI and playback endpoint (Design + ENG) (W3-4).
- Pilot with two enterprise customers, gather feedback and acceptance (W5).

Acceptance criteria:
- PM can request a region-scoped evidence bundle via API and Console with a signed manifest.
- Retention simulator returns predicted artifact set for test cases (unit + e2e).
- Audit-playback shows artifact preview and provenance metadata in Console.
- Security review completed and KMS integration documented.
